What to look for in summer jackets

  • Laminated beats drop-liner. A bonded waterproof membrane keeps the outer from soaking through and chilling you in sustained rain.
  • CE Level 2 armour. Insist on shoulder and elbow protectors, and budget for a back protector if one is not included.
  • Layering system. A removable thermal liner turns one jacket into a three-season solution for British weather.
  • Connection zip. A jacket-to-trouser zip stops your kit separating in a slide — buy matching pieces where possible.

Frequently asked questions

How much should I spend on summer jackets?

Our catalogue spans £149.95 to £512.96. Budget options under £150 cover the essentials, the £150–£400 mid-range hits the sweet spot for most UK tourers, and premium picks above £400 add refinement, lighter materials and longer-term durability.

Which brands are worth considering?

Popular, well-reviewed brands in this category include Alpinestars, Rev'it, Held. All are stocked by SportsBikeShop with UK warranty support.

Textile or leather?

Textile is the practical all-weather choice for UK touring thanks to waterproof membranes and thermal liners. Leather offers the best abrasion resistance for spirited, dry-weather sport touring. Many riders own both.

faq.q: Are mesh jackets safe in a crash?
faq.a: Yes, provided you choose a quality mesh jacket with CE-certified armour and abrasion-resistant panels. Perforated leather options like the Alpinestars Missile V3 offer track-grade protection while still flowing air. Textile mesh jackets use tough constructions and armour at the shoulders and elbows. As always, look for a CE garment rating and fit the armour snugly over your joints.

Perforated leather, as on the Alpinestars Missile V3 and GP Plus R V4, gives the best abrasion resistance and suits sporty riders who want cooling on track and fast roads. Textile mesh jackets like the Rev'it Airwave 4 are lighter, cheaper and more relaxed for commuting and town riding. Choose leather for outright protection, textile for value and everyday comfort.

faq.q: Will I stay dry in a mesh jacket?
faq.a: No. The whole point of a mesh jacket is to let air flow straight through, so it offers almost no waterproofing or wind protection. In the UK you should always pack a lightweight waterproof over-jacket to pull on when a shower arrives. Some riders keep the mesh jacket for guaranteed hot spells and switch to a laminated jacket when rain is forecast.

faq.q: How cold is too cold for a mesh jacket?
faq.a: Mesh jackets are designed for warm weather, roughly the high teens Celsius and above. Below that the constant airflow quickly chills you, especially at motorway speed. A thin windproof layer underneath can extend the range a little, but once temperatures drop you are better off in a three-season textile jacket with a thermal liner.

faq.q: Can I add a back protector?
faq.a: Most quality summer jackets include shoulder and elbow armour and a pocket for a back protector, though the back insert is often sold separately. Adding a CE Level 2 back protector is strongly recommended, as the back is a vulnerable area. Check the jacket has a full-length back pocket and buy an insert sized to fit it.
